# Fusion Conductor

> A main agent that plans and reviews without editing files, and a cheaper sidekick that executes. A one-line opencode plugin with mechanical edit deny at the permission layer. Inspired by Cognition's Devin Fusion pattern. Forked from opencode-fusion. Independent project - not affiliated with Cognition, Devin, or OpenCode.

Fusion Conductor is an *opencode plugin* (not an app). Install it by adding one line to `opencode.json`, restart opencode, and the main agent delegates edits to the sidekick.

## Quick install

Recommended: `opencode plugin add opencode-fusion-conductor`. It installs the package and writes the config entry into the global config itself, failing with a real error if the install fails.

Manual alternative: add one line to your opencode config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, or a project-level `opencode.json`):

```json
{
  "plugins": [{ "package": "opencode-fusion-conductor@2.0.0", "options": { "profile": "opencode-go" } }]
}
```

Then fully quit and restart opencode (or `opencode service restart`). There is no skill and no installer. The plugin injects the agent team and the `/conductor` command on the next launch; a bare `/conductor` on an unconfigured install runs the first-run setup interview in chat. Uninstall by removing the line and restarting.

Silent-failure note: a plugin install that fails leaves opencode running with stock agents. Check `opencode plugin list` for the `opencode-fusion-conductor` id, inspect `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`, and retry via the `opencode plugin add ...` CLI, which surfaces install errors directly.

Coming from opencode-fusion? Say `undo fusion` with the old fusion-setup skill first to remove the file-based install, then add the plugin line. `/conductor` warns if leftover fusion files are detected.

## Core ideas for agents helping users

1. Main (`build`) plans, delegates, and reviews — it must not edit files. `plan` is the plan-mode primary; `sidekick` executes edits and commands.
2. Sidekick executes precise specs; explore/research/design/reviewer/vision are the other injected roles. `explore` is opencode's built-in read-only agent, model-only. Set `experimental.subagent_depth` to at least 2 yourself if you want the sidekick to keep delegating read-only lookups (V2 exposes no such knob to plugins).
3. OpenCode enforces this with ordered `permissions` arrays registered by the plugin (edit deny + subagent graph), plus a session hook that strips edit/write/patch/grep/glob from build/plan model requests - so "won't delegate" means visible inaction, never a silent bypass.
4. Config loads at startup — restart after changing plugin options. The agent registry is materialized at startup, so model changes require a restart (a platform limitation).
5. Cross-vendor review is emergent: pick main and sidekick from different model families.
6. Only the permission layer is enforced; prompts are advisory. Ignoring them costs quality or tokens, never an unauthorized edit.
7. If the sidekick misses a spec twice, the main agent dictates the exact patch verbatim (file, line range, code) for the sidekick to apply — the retry loop cannot deadlock. If the dictated patch fails verification, the plan is wrong and main revises it.
8. Provider API keys belong in environment variables: opencode.json supports `{env:VAR}` and `{file:path}` substitution, so a key never sits in plaintext config or passes through the chat. An unset variable resolves to an empty string, which surfaces as auth errors.
9. The `/conductor` slash command reports or edits the plugin's own options: `/conductor` with no args runs `conductor_status` (read-only report including leftover fusion-install hazards); with args it runs `conductor_configure` (role=model pairs, `profile <name>`, or `audit=true`/`claude=true` flags), writing a backup at `opencode.json.conductor-backup` and telling you to restart.
10. Bundled subscription profiles (`opencode-go`, `opencode-zen`, `opencode-zen-free`, `chatgpt`, `github-copilot`) are applied via the `profile` option; the `models` option overrides per role. Provider auth stays out-of-band via `opencode auth login` — profiles never contain keys.
11. The `audit` option (boolean, off by default) enables a hook that logs the delegation tree and per-agent token usage. The `claude` option (boolean, off by default) enables the Claude Code bridge tools `conductor_claude_status`/`conductor_claude_review`, which require the Claude Pro/Max CLI installed and authenticated.
12. Targets OpenCode V2 (2.x) since the 2.0.0 port: agents register through `ctx.agent.transform` upserts, permissions are V2 ordered arrays (`bash` -> `shell`, `task` -> `subagent`), and the `/conductor` tools read and write both the V1 `plugin` tuple form and the native V2 `plugins` object form.
13. First-run setup: a bare `/conductor` on an unconfigured install (no profile, no model overrides) runs a setup interview - profile choice from the status report's available-profiles list, per-role model overrides, and optional `audit`/`claude` flags - then applies the answers via `conductor_configure` and tells you to restart. Passing arguments directly applies them and skips the interview.
14. Plugin updates: `opencode plugin check`, then `opencode plugin update opencode-fusion-conductor`. Restart after.
15. Removal: `opencode plugin remove opencode-fusion-conductor`, then restart.
16. Model changes require a restart: the agent registry is materialized at startup, so injected agents and their model assignments only take effect on the next launch.
